title: Amazon’s Decart acquisition aims to narrow AI chip gap with Nvidia
summary: Amazon acquires Decart to narrow its AI chip gap with Nvidia
detailed: Amazon agreed to acquire the technology behind AI startup Decart and its founding team for approximately $7.5 billion.
The deal covers the Decart Optimization Stack (DOS) software tool to optimize AI models across different hardware, while excluding Decart's AI models.
Amazon aims to use the optimization technology to improve the performance of its Trainium chips as it competes with Nvidia hardware and scales AWS data centers.
sentences: Amazon has agreed to acquire the technology behind artificial intelligence startup Decart, along with its founding team, for approximately $7.5 billion, according to Bloomberg.
The deal covers the Decart Optimization Stack (DOS), a software tool designed to optimize AI model performance across different types of hardware, as well as Decart’s researchers and engineers.
However, Amazon is not acquiring Decart’s AI models.

According to TechCrunch, there appears to be broad industry consensus that Decart’s technology for optimizing AI models to run on non-Nvidia chips is worth several billion dollars.

Anthropic had also reportedly attempted to acquire the startup for a similar amount, while Nvidia, which participated in Decart’s $300 million funding round at a $4 billion valuation, was rumored to be a prospective buyer.
Amazon’s deal will bring on board Decart co-founders Dean Leitersdorf, Orian Leitersdorf and Moshe Shalev, along with their team.

By incorporating the startup’s optimization technology, Amazon hopes to improve the performance of its Trainium chips as it seeks to turn Amazon Web Services (AWS) into a $1 trillion revenue business.
Amazon said in its announcement that it has worked with Decart since 2025 to optimize its Trainium chips.
The deal is aimed at accelerating that work, potentially allowing Amazon to offer its Trainium-based data centers, which Anthropic already uses, to a broader customer base.
Amazon CEO Andy Jassy plans to begin offering Trainium chips next year to other companies that build data centers, according to Bloomberg.
AWS cloud customers can already access the chips.
Amazon has been working to simplify the adoption of Trainium, positioning its chips as an alternative to Nvidia hardware, which powers most AI models.
Previous reports, citing people familiar with the matter, indicated that Anthropic was in talks to acquire Decart for approximately $6 billion.
Had the acquisition gone ahead, it would have been Anthropic’s largest deal.

Decart said in May that it had raised $300 million in a funding round led by Radical Ventures, with participation from Nvidia Corp., Atreides Management, Valor Equity Partners and Adobe Ventures.

Existing investors Sequoia Capital, Benchmark and Zeev Ventures also participated in the round, which valued the startup at nearly $4 billion, according to The Wall Street Journal, up from $3.1 billion in August 2025.
